items.title: IRGC claims strikes on U.S. Patriot system, bases in 95th attack wave

featured_image.name: US, Israeli targets struck in mass IRGC missile, drone strikes

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced on Friday that its forces struck U.S. military positions on Bubiyan Island in Kuwait and a Patriot air defense system in northern Bahrain as part of the 95th wave of its Operation True Promise 4 campaign, marking the latest escalation in a war now entering its sixth week.

items.title: Zelensky meets Erdogan in Istanbul for ceasefire talks

featured_image.name: Turkish President Erdogan welcomes President of Ukraine Zelenskyy in Istanbul

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Istanbul on Saturday for security talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, with discussions centered on ceasefire efforts and the broader diplomatic push known as the Istanbul Process. The meeting at the Dolmabahçe Palace comes at a sensitive moment, just one day after Erdogan held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.[1][2][3]

items.title: UAE intercepts 79 Iranian projectiles as strikes batter Gulf infrastructure

featured_image.name: UAE considers striking Iranian missile sites as regional war ...

items.description:
The UAE Ministry of Defence said on Saturday that its air defense systems intercepted 23 ballistic missiles and 56 drones launched from Iran on April 4, marking another day of sustained aerial bombardment against the Gulf state. The latest wave brings the total number of projectiles engaged since the conflict began on February 28 to 498 ballistic missiles, 23 cruise missiles, and 2,141 drones.[1]

The attacks, which began after coordinated U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February, have inflicted mounting damage on the UAE's energy and industrial infrastructure, raising questions about the long-term economic toll even as air defenses continue to neutralize the vast majority of incoming threats.[2]

items.title: US burns through critical weapons stockpiles five weeks into Iran war

featured_image.name: Lockheed Martin delivers 900th THAAD interceptor to U.S. Missile Defense  Agency

items.description: Five weeks into Operation Epic Fury, the United States and Israel have unleashed devastating firepower on Iran, striking more than 11,000 targets and claiming a 90% reduction in Tehran's missile and drone attacks. Yet Iran's low-cost, high-disruption approach to the conflict has exposed a stark vulnerability in Western military doctrine: expensive, precision-guided weapons systems are being consumed at unsustainable rates to counter cheap, mass-produced threats.[1][2][3]

items.title: Bangladesh, Thailand impose emergency measures as energy crisis deepens

featured_image.name: Bangladesh Enforces Austerity as Energy Crisis Deepens

items.description: Bangladesh and Thailand are rolling out emergency measures to combat a worsening energy crisis fueled by conflict in the Middle East, with Dhaka slashing work hours and Bangkok confronting warnings of construction industry collapse as diesel prices nearly triple on global markets.

items.title: Iran's radar-silent missile systems down US jets, exposing electronic warfare gap
items.description: Iran's downing of a U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle and strike on an A-10 Thunderbolt on Friday marked the first loss of manned American aircraft to enemy fire during Operation Epic Fury, exposing what analysts say is a critical vulnerability in U.S. electronic warfare: the inability to counter heat-seeking, radar-silent air defense systems.

items.title: Global services sector contracts for first time in 3 years amid Iran war oil shock

featured_image.name: Iran war-hit oil prices will soon rise if Hormuz stays shut - CNBC

items.description: A month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, the economic consequences are cascading across the globe. Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has collapsed by 95%, according to a United Nations Conference on Trade and Development report released on April 2, choking off roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply and sending energy prices surging. The S&P Global Services PMI fell to 49.8 in March 2026, slipping below the 50.0 threshold that separates expansion from contraction for the first time in more than three years.[1][2][3]

items.title: China pushes five-point peace plan as Iran war nears fifth week

featured_image.name: Will China join Pakistan-led efforts to mediate US-Iran peace?

items.description: As the US-Israeli war against Iran enters its fifth week with no end in sight, China has emerged as the most active diplomatic player pushing for a ceasefire, while the conflict's disruption of global energy supplies sends shockwaves through economies from Manila to Seoul.

items.title: U.S. Dollar Index hits highest level since May 2025

featured_image.name: Trump officially nominates Kevin Warsh as Federal chair - CNBC

items.description: The US Dollar Index climbed to its highest level since May 2025, crossing the 100.08 mark on April 3, 2026, as a confluence of geopolitical turmoil and shifting Federal Reserve expectations drove investors into the greenback. The rally marks a sharp reversal from late 2025, when the index languished in the mid-90s, and is now reshaping currency markets worldwide.[1][2]

items.title: Pakistan reverses record fuel hike as Asia reels from Iran war energy crisis

featured_image.name: Pak cuts petrol price by Rs 80 per litre after protest over sharp hike

items.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, triggered by the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran that began on February 28, is sending shockwaves through import-dependent economies across Asia and the developing world. From the Philippines to Pakistan to Vietnam, governments are scrambling to contain fuel shortages, record price spikes, and currency crises that threaten to derail economic growth across the region.
